title: Four-layer scanner evaluation
description:
Purpose: Grade the scanner in four layers and expand the dataflow graph so a data item is a thing, not a string on an edge. Plexus is the runner, not a fifth kind of finding.

Terms we keep: component, data flow, data item.
Terms for a line: mention, evidence, or span. Do not say "data item reference."
Today's data_items eval (T0/T1, PR #15) is mention-level. If data item means the entity, that layer must be renamed or split.

Four grades:
1. Raw pattern hits: did a YAML heuristic fire before classification. YAML is the rulebook, not a picture of the repo.
2. Components and data flows: did we build the right map (boxes and arrows).
3. Data items: the unique personal-data thing across files.
4. Mentions / evidence spans: the line where we saw a thing.

What exists now:
- Graph nodes are only asset, actor, third_party_service. Edges are data_flow. Lines are receipts.
- Mention-level CLI grade (T1) is on develop.
- 15 proposed component notes (PR #16). No data-flow gold packets.
- Plexus evaluate accuracy is Yes/No span overlap on field notes, not a component or flow scorecard.
- .rs files are ingested (PR #17). There is no Rust analyzer.

Exclusions: implementing precision (that stays the existing precision initiative); merging to main; accepting gold without a human.

Definition of done for this initiative: children cover ontology, the four grades, and how Plexus runs each grade. Linked from DATAP-602.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text: Four-layer eval follows the eval harness into the scanner project (KDATAP-4f6956 / KDATAP-3ee2c2). Do not keep building new eval layers only in the CLI repo.
